arxiv-2111-07447.title: Learning Multi-Stage Tasks with One Demonstration via Self-Replay
arxiv-2111-07447.creator: Norman Di Palo, Edward Jonhs
arxiv-2111-07447.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce a novel method to learn everyday-like multi-stage tasks from a single human demonstration, without requiring any prior object knowledge. Inspired by the recent Coarse-to-Fine Imitation Learning method, we model imitation learning as a learned object reaching phase followed by an open-loop replay of the demonstrator’s actions.

arxiv-2112-04144.description: Abstract In this paper, we study inhomogeneous Diophantine approximation over the completion K v K_{v} of a global function field K K (over a finite field) for a discrete valuation v v , with affine algebra R v R_{v} .

arxiv-2203-00633.title: Transformer Grammars: Augmenting Transformer Language Models with Syntactic Inductive Biases at Scale
arxiv-2203-00633.creator: Laurent Sartran Samuel Barrett Adhiguna Kuncoro, Miloš Stanojević Phil Blunsom Chris Dyer
arxiv-2203-00633.description: Abstract We introduce Transformer Grammars (TGs), a novel class of Transformer language models that combine (i) the expressive power, scalability, and strong performance of Transformers and (ii) recursive syntactic compositions, which here are implemented through a special attention mask and deterministic transformation of the linearized tree.

arxiv-2205-09588.title: How catastrophic can catastrophic forgetting be in linear regression?
arxiv-2205-09588.creator: Itay Evron, Edward Moroshko, Rachel Ward, Nati Srebro, Daniel Soudry
arxiv-2205-09588.description: Abstract To better understand catastrophic forgetting, we study fitting an overparameterized linear model to a sequence of tasks with different input distributions. We analyze how much the model forgets the true labels of earlier tasks after training on subsequent tasks, obtaining exact expressions and bounds.

arxiv-2206-05046.title: Tensorization of p p -weak Differentiable structures
arxiv-2206-05046.creator: Sylvester Eriksson-Bique, Tapio Rajala, Elefterios Soultanis
arxiv-2206-05046.description: Abstract . We consider p p -weak differentiable structures that were recently introduced in [ 9 ] , and prove that the product of p p -weak charts is a p p -weak chart. This implies that the product of two spaces with a p p -weak differentiable structure also admits a p p -weak differentiable structure.

arxiv-2206-14884.title: Composite scalar boson mass dependence on the constituent mass anomalous dimension
arxiv-2206-14884.creator: A. Doff a and A. A. Natale b
arxiv-2206-14884.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by A. Doff a and A. A. Natale b. We perform a Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) evaluation of composite scalar boson masses in order to verify how these masses can be smaller than the composition scale. The calculation is developed with a constituent self-energy dependent on its mass anomalous dimension ( γ \gamma ), and we obtain a relation showing how the scalar mass decreases as γ \gamma is increased.

arxiv-2402-16840.title: MobiLlama: Towards Accurate and Lightweight Fully Transparent GPT
arxiv-2402-16840.creator: Omkar Thawakar, Ashmal Vayani, Salman Khan, Hisham Cholakal, Rao M. Anwer, Michael Felsberg, Tim Baldwin, Eric P. Xing, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, [0.25cm] Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI, Australian National University, Aalto University, The University of Melbourne, Linköping University
arxiv-2402-16840.description: Abstract ‘ Bigger the better ’ has been the predominant trend in recent Large Language Models (LLMs) development. However, LLMs do not suit well for scenarios that require on-device processing, energy efficiency, low memory footprint, and response efficiency. These requisites are crucial for privacy, security, and sustainable deployment.

arxiv-2404-13971.title: HamilToniQ: An Open-Source Benchmark Toolkit for Quantum Computers Thanks: The first two authors contributed equally to this work.
arxiv-2404-13971.creator: Xiaotian Xu, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Robert Wille
arxiv-2404-13971.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce HamilToniQ, an open-source, and application-oriented benchmarking toolkit for the comprehensive evaluation of Quantum Processing Units (QPUs). Designed to navigate the complexities of quantum computations, HamilToniQ incorporates a methodological framework assessing QPU types, topologies, and multi-QPU systems.

arxiv-2407-20358.title: low-alpha operation of the iota storage ring
arxiv-2407-20358.creator: M. Wallbank, J. Jarvis, Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory, Batavia, IL, USA
arxiv-2407-20358.description: Abstract Operation with ultra-low momentum-compaction factor (alpha) is a desirable capability for many storage rings and synchrotron radiation sources. For example, low-alpha lattices are commonly used to produce picosecond bunches for the generation of coherent THz radiation and are the basis of a number of conceptual designs for EUV generation via steady-state microbunching (SSMB).

arxiv-2408-09572.title: Local Rigidity of the Bergman Metric and of the Kähler Carathéodory Metric
arxiv-2408-09572.creator: Robert Xin Dong, Ruoyi Wang, and, Bun Wong
arxiv-2408-09572.description: Abstract We prove that if the Carathéodory metric on a strictly pseudoconvex domain with a smooth boundary is locally Kähler near the boundary, then the domain is biholomorphic to a ball. We also establish a local rigidity theorem for domains with Bergman metrics of constant holomorphic sectional curvature, and highlight this relationship with the Lu constant. † † footnotetext: Keywords.

arxiv-2501-06894.title: Analyzing the Evolution and Maintenance of Quantum Software Repositories
arxiv-2501-06894.creator: Krishna Upadhyay 1 , Vinaik Chhetri 1 , A.B. Siddique 2 , Umar Farooq 1
arxiv-2501-06894.description: Abstract Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, but quantum software development faces significant challenges, including a steep learning curve, high hardware error rates, and a lack of mature engineering practices. This study conducts a large-scale mining analysis of over 21,000 GitHub repositories, containing 1.2 million commits from more than 10,000 developers, to examine the evolution and maintenance of quantum software.

arxiv-2503-14653.title: Meson Mixing Bounds on Z ′ Z^{\prime} Mass in the Alignment Limit: Establishing the Phenomenological Viability of the 331 Model

pmc-13275127.title: sc-rDSeq: Droplet-based single-cell full-length total RNA-seq method
pmc-13275127.creator: Xue Sun, Oren Ram
pmc-13275127.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This protocol describes sc‑rDSeq, a scalable, droplet‑based method for full‑length, strand‑specific total RNA sequencing at single‑cell resolution. The protocol uses a refined set of 220 ribosomal‑depleted sequences (rDS) primers that selectively exclude ribosomal RNA during initial reverse transcription, enabling capture of both polyadenylated and non‑polyadenylated RNAs such as histone RNAs, noncoding RNAs, and enhancer RNAs, without requiring costly post‑amplification depletion steps.

pmc-13339638.title: Spherical Boundary Conditions: A Topological Framework for Isotropic Collective Dynamics
pmc-13339638.creator: Manuel Dedola, Ludovico Cademartiri
pmc-13339638.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Standard periodic boundary conditions (PBC) impose a toroidal topology on simulation domains. While geometrically flat, this topology allows for coherent reentrant self-interactions that preserve spurious long-range temporal correlations. We show that these topological artifacts manifest as strong, lattice-aligned anisotropy in collective dynamic observables, rendering scalar relaxation rates direction-dependent even at near-particle length scales, thereby violating the static–dynamic correspondence of isotropic liquids (de Gennes narrowing).
